findings.text: _merged_requeue keeps the points on the pointer but takes the new record's dispatch_options wholesale at reckon/crew/runs.py:965, and reckon/crew/dispatching/launch.py:444 reads a launched run's priority from those options, so a reprioritised request that a coordinator re-dispatches naming no points is ranked and charged at 7 while the run it becomes records priority 0 and its review inherits nothing. The points survive the budget and are lost at launch, which is the figure the requeue's own comment says it preserves.

the added review-charge test passes priority_budget=10 to queue_dispatch itself, while the two production sites that queue a composed review — reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:732 and :796 — call queue_dispatch with no budget, so a review whose points ride _queued_request_record is stored uncharged on that path; the test's claim that a review cannot hold the budget and leave it available is true only of a caller that supplies the budget.

the landing record's only measure still reads 'Measure, at revision 522df5161d ... 10 passed, EXIT=0', naming a revision and a test count that predate the repairs the same record's Repair round paragraph claims are landed; a reader comparing it with the manifest's 14 passed at 0e35e05838 finds the plan-facing record describing a tree the node no longer ships.

the repaired accessor is the expression queue_order._priority already defines at reckon/crew/queue_order.py:240-242, so the repository keeps two named spellings of one definition; calling _priority would leave the queue's own name as the single place the points a request carries are turned into a number.
